exposure: Emergency cesarean section vs. spontaneous delivery
Personality traits (emotional stability, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness, openness)
Preterm delivery vs. no preterm delivery
Anesthesia during delivery vs. no anesthesia
cohort: Pregnant women from the Maternal Anxiety in Relation to Infant Development (MARI) Study
finding: Lower emotional stability, conscientiousness, and openness were associated with worse subjective birth experiences, particularly in the presence of unexpected incidents during delivery such as preterm delivery, emergency cesarean section, and the need for anesthesia.
mod_finding: Women with lower emotional stability had worse subjective birth experiences after an emergency cesarean section compared to those with higher emotional stability.
followup_time: Within the first 10 days after delivery
